text.p: Germany's Commerzbank AG on Wednesday denied a report it planned to sell its stake in vehicle components maker Kolbenschmidt AG to a unit of Metallgesellschaft.
A spokesman for Germany's third largest bank said its 49.99 percent stake in Kolbenschmidt, which has a Frankfurt bourse listing, would remain in its hands for the time being.
The bank added that British engineering group T&N Plc was still interested in the stake and confirmed that the option that T&N has on the holding was valid until the end of the year.

A spokesman for diversified industrial Metallgesellschaft, which once owned part of Kolbenschmidt, had already on Tuesday denied the report in the German Boersenzeitung newspaper that its Metallbank unit was interested in the stake.

T&N, which already owns German piston ring maker Goetze, had until now been prevented from buying the stake by the German cartel office on the grounds that it would give it too much control of the German pistons market.
An appeal against the cartel office decision has been lodged with a Berlin court.
